messages:
Priya Desai: Hey finance folks — got a customer saying their Feb invoice didn’t apply the $5k credit we promised (from the outage goodwill). Invoice already sent. Can someone sanity check timing + what we can do to remediate?

Support Bot: Ticket created: SUP-28490 “missing credit application on Feb invoice” (link: https://jira.redwoodinference.dev/browse/SUP-28490)

Emily Stone: Yep, looking. What’s the account + invoice number?

Priya Desai: ZenChat. Invoice `INV-2026-02-1147` (sent this morning). Credit was approved last week by Jordan. They’re asking us to re-issue the invoice with the credit applied.

Mei Lin: Quick note: if the credit was created after the invoice draft was finalized, it won’t net on that invoice. It’ll apply to the next invoice unless we do an adjustment/credit note.

Emily Stone: I pulled the ledger entry. Credit exists but “effective_at” is 2026-02-21 18:12 UTC, invoice was finalized 2026-02-21 16:40 UTC. So it missed the application window.

Priya Desai: Ah. Customer expectation was “this month’s invoice.” What are our options that won’t cause a mess for RevRec?

Rishi Malhotra: Prefer not to void/reissue unless absolutely required. Re-issuing changes the close package + audit trail. Safer path: issue a credit memo / adjustment that nets on next invoice, and (if needed) refund now.

Cole Summers: +1. Technically we can create an “invoice adjustment” line item in the billing system tied to the original invoice (doesn’t touch usage lines). It’ll show as a standalone credit note referencing INV-2026-02-1147.

Emily Stone: Options (in order of preference):
1) Create a credit note for $5,000 referencing INV-2026-02-1147. Customer keeps original invoice; credit note reduces A/R. (Best for audit.)
2) If they insist on netting immediately, apply the credit note and also mark as “paid” net of credit (depends on how they pay).
3) Refund method only if they already paid gross and need cash back.

Priya Desai: They haven’t paid yet, payment terms net-30. They mainly want the paperwork to reflect the credit.

Mei Lin: Then credit note is perfect. Also: make sure Support messaging is clear that usage meters are unchanged — this is purely credit timing.

Priya Desai: Great. How fast can we issue the credit note?

Emily Stone: I can do today. Need confirmation the $5k is approved + what memo text should say.

Priya Desai: Approval is in the sales email thread. I’ll paste excerpt + link in the ticket. Suggested memo: “Service credit per goodwill adjustment; applies to account ZenChat; references INV-2026-02-1147.”

Rishi Malhotra: Add internal note: “approved by CRO; goodwill credit; non-recurring.” Helps later when auditors ask why.

Cole Summers: One more thing: if the customer is on autopay, the credit note won’t stop the autopay run unless Finance updates the collection schedule. Emily, flag if ZenChat is on autopay.

Emily Stone: Confirmed not on autopay. I’ll issue credit note EOD and attach PDF to SUP-28490.

Laura Bennett: Please also tag this as a process gap — we keep hitting “credit created after invoice finalize.” If we can set a cutoff + comms for sales/support, it’ll reduce churn from billing surprises.

Priya Desai: :thumbsup: I’ll add a checklist item for Support: verify invoice status before promising “applies to this invoice.” Also will route to Talia to incorporate into month-end freeze guidance.

Emily Stone: Action items:
- Emily: issue $5k credit note referencing INV-2026-02-1147 + update ticket
- Priya: customer response (explain timing + attach credit note once ready)
- Rishi/Laura: decide if we need a policy note for “credits cutoff vs invoice finalize”

Priya Desai: Thanks all. I’ll tell customer we’ll send a credit note today and it’ll net their balance due accordingly.
